correctness.rationale: Center iid X1,X2 at mean μ and write Z1,Z2 with mgf M. Conditional mean zero given |Z1-Z2| annihilates (Z1+Z2)cosh(t(Z2-Z1)); exchangeability independently annihilates the sinh part. Factoring expectation of (Z1+Z2)e^{t(Z2-Z1)} using independence yields M'(-t)M(t)+M(-t)M'(t)=0. Thus for K=log M, K'(t)+K'(-t)=0 and K(t)=K(-t) near zero. MGF uniqueness forces central symmetry. Conversely global sign reversal leaves separation invariant and flips midpoint, proving conditional mean constant. Exponential integrability justifies differentiation on smaller neighborhood. Independent exhaustive exact fractions confirmed 9072 support-weight laws, 396 equivalent cases; enumeration is not the universal proof.

value.rationale: Mean independence of two-observation midpoint and separation is a canonical and weaker dependence constraint than full independence. The theorem gives a complete symmetry characterization under a transparent local mgf assumption and includes atomic, mixed and continuous parents, sharply separating symmetry tests from classical sample-mean/range normality independence theorems.

limitations: Only iid n=2, any law with finite mgf near zero. Characterizes central symmetry, not normality or independence.
